Blended matter, etc. — if flour is called wet in wet or dry in dry — Tosafot disagreed; and in chapter HaOrlah they wrote two versions that contradict each other: for one explanation it is wet in wet, and for another resolution it is dry in dry. Since I need to learn from this, I will copy the matter briefly: we say in chapter Meshilin on the mishnah — a woman who borrowed from her friend water and salt according to their usual practice — and the Gemara challenges: let water and salt be nullified relative to the dough! It answers: behold a kav of wheat became mixed for him in ten kabin of his friend's wheat — let the other eat and rejoice! They laughed at this — what is different about wheat in barley that it is not nullified? Wheat in wheat too — for R' Yehudah it is not nullified, etc. — end. Tosafot challenged in chapter HaOrlah daf 82 s.v. R' Yehudah: behold dry in dry, even in its kind, is nullified for R' Yehudah! And Tosafot answered: it deals with flour in flour — for otherwise wheat would be recognizable in barley, and how do we say it is nullified? And another answer: flour in flour, since it is cold, is dry in dry and nullified; only there it deals with hot substances, etc., and the taste is wet in wet — end. From this comes the dispute mentioned. In truth, in my humble opinion the second explanation of Tosafot appears correct; and Maharshal and Maharsha raised difficulties — Maharsha challenged: behold Tosafot themselves distinguish between money that is not nullified because "its owner is upon it," and issur that is nullified — so what does the Gemara mean "wheat in barley, no" — that it is not its kind and nullified; from where do we know this? Only in issur, but in money where its owner is upon it, even when not its kind it is not nullified — he forced to resolve it. And Maharshal challenged plainly: when it says "wheat in barley, no" — that not its kind is nullified — it still challenges well from water and salt that they should be nullified relative to dough, for that is not its kind! However, for the second answer above — requires study: for Tosafot proved it does not deal with flour — for then wheat in barley would also be called same kind in its kind; only actual wheat and barley, and hot substances that absorb each other — then barley is recognizable and returns; as Tosafot wrote — only the entire matter is about the taste wheat received from barley; if so the Gemara says well that it is nullified, and Maharsha's difficulty about "its owner is upon it" does not apply, for we do not judge the body of barley but its taste, and taste alone — "its owner is upon it" does not apply at all; and but for the Torah's amplification in service of the Holy One that taste is not like the essence, from the Torah one would say "its owner is upon it" for money; but wheat in wheat where wheat bodies became mixed — they are not recognizable and also received taste — "its owner is upon it" applies well, for there is his friend's in substance; and Maharshal's difficulty is also resolved: even though wheat in barley are nullified, meaning "its owner" does not apply to taste alone and wheat bodies return as stated — but in water and salt mixed in dough and irremovable, plainly "its owner is upon it"; if so the second answer appears correct. Behold Ram of Lublin noticed in Tosafot that they wrote it deals with hot substances — and his explanation is as above, that it does not deal with flour in flour; in truth he removed wheat and asked why wheat in barley is nullified — is there not taste and not its kind, taste forbids! And he wrote in these words that not its kind — taste is nullified for R' Yehudah, etc. — end; and Maran's conversation I do not know, for not its kind — does taste forbid for R' Yehudah? From where this, that R' Yehudah certainly holds d'oraisa? Perhaps he holds like Ran that we do not say taste is like essence except where the issur body dissolved in heter, i.e. milk in grits; but if the issur was drawn out and only its taste remains — that is its taste and not its substance and is not forbidden d'oraisa; or one may say in tehumim they were lenient as Tosafot wrote in several places; or R' Yehudah holds even d'rabbanan it is permitted, and there is proof from mishnah Terumot chapter 10: R' Yehudah — all that are cooked together are permitted except meat — and therefore in not its kind it deals, for in its kind R' Yehudah does not nullify — learn that in not its kind he holds like Ran that taste does not forbid even d'rabbanan, only in meat whose taste is strong. Accordingly, for the first answer in Tosafot that it deals with flour in flour called wet in wet — the difficulty in Bava Metzia: a kav of wheat in ten kabin of barley — why nullified? Is it not its kind wet in wet in dough, and here there is a mixture of issur and forbids for all! And to say ten kabin is not precise but more — is strained; the Gemara should immediately say from where sixty or seventy! Therefore it must deal with same kind in its kind that is not nullified — specifically wet in wet; and the reason Tosafot wrote: regarding matter that mixes throughout all the heter and does not stand by itself — even flour mixes well and does not stand by itself — what difference if flour is hot or cold; but regarding taste like essence in not its kind wet in wet — hot wet in wet that mixes completely in heter; but flour in flour, since it is cold, does not give taste in heter and does not mix so much as to make heter issur, for each crumb of flour stands by itself and is not like wine and oil as Rambam wrote — therefore taste like essence does not apply. Therefore in Beitzah regarding same kind in its kind that does not nullify for R' Yehudah — even flour in flour is called wet in wet and is not nullified; but in not its kind where mixture issur is from the law of taste like essence — for this purpose cold is not called wet in wet to forbid. If so Tosafot's words are well explained: it deals with flour in flour, and regarding same kind in its kind flour in flour is wet in wet and not nullified for R' Yehudah; but wheat in barley are nullified, for it is not its kind, and on account of taste like essence it does not forbid, for regarding giving taste flour in flour is called dry, for it is cold and there is no concern of noten ta'am. If so it appears for practical ruling: same kind in its kind where flour mixed in flour — one may be lenient in a place of loss, since many poskim hold it is called dry in dry; and even according to Tosafot it is called wet in wet only regarding R' Yehudah's matter that same kind in its kind is not nullified — but not regarding taste like essence; and same kind in its kind, whatever it may be wet in wet — this is also d'oraisa nullified in majority, only they forbade it by decree; in not its kind too it is possible there is no noten ta'am, therefore there is no stringency concern, and Rambam is worthy to rely on him; and especially this flour in flour called wet in wet as above — R' Yehudah holds same kind in its kind is not nullified, meaning wet in wet as stated; and this itself has no absolute foundation, for all the necessity is that R' Yehudah holds terumah in one in a hundred in its kind, and likewise in split nuts R' Yehudah holds it is not nullified; and Tosafot challenged: behold otherwise same kind in its kind is not nullified — therefore Tosafot were forced to distinguish wet in wet from dry in dry; and besides they also resolved Tosafot's version and Rashi's in any case — there is easy resolution: for we challenge in Chullin 92b on R' Yehudah who said fish brine in two hundred — and we challenge: did R' Yehudah not say same kind in its kind is not nullified? And we answer: brine is different, for it is only sweat — and Tosafot s.v. She'ani explained: and it is forbidden only d'rabbanan; and so Rashba in his novellae — brine is d'rabbanan that forbids; and in their words R' Yehudah did not say same kind in its kind is not nullified. And in that sugya of a litra of dried figs in Zevachim chapter HaTa'aruvot it implies R' Yehudah holds terumah is d'rabbanan, especially in fruits for all it is d'rabbanan — if so on account of same kind in its kind, behold in d'rabbanan it is nullified; and likewise kilaei hakerem for those who hold terumah is d'rabbanan when kedushat ha'aretz was nullified — even kilaei hakerem is d'rabbanan as Tosafot wrote in Zevachim beginning chapter Kol HaZevachim and Yevamot 81 — see there; if so that of pomegranates in Dan is established entirely in terumah and kilaei hakerem which is d'rabbanan, and same kind in its kind is nullified — therefore they needed to say on account of their importance it is not nullified — requires study on Tosafot who did not mention this. In truth one must understand in that sugya in Beitzah mentioned where we say wheat in wheat too — for R' Yehudah it is not nullified; behold issur of tehumim which we establish is only d'rabbanan as Tosafot wrote — if so in d'rabbanan behold same kind in its kind is nullified for R' Yehudah — requires study apparently. What resolves this in brief: we do not say two leniencies — for here there is davar sheyesh lo matirin that is not nullified; and if it were d'rabbanan, behold regarding sheylo yimatzu we judge it like d'oraisa as we say in chapter 1 of Beitzah that safek of davar sheyesh lo matirin is forbidden like Torah law — only tehumim is different, for they were more lenient in it. And behold further: davar sheyesh lo matirin is not nullified — behold it is davar sheyesh lo matirin, and in sheylo yimatzu even in a thousand it is not nullified — must also say here since it is tehumim they were more lenient than other sheylo yimatzu that it is nullified; if so behold two leniencies in tehumim — we do not say such leniencies; investigate — therefore the correct practice is as I wrote:
One in two is nullified; and if two in three became mixed — Shach and Pri Chadash elaborated that likewise it is nullified, and all the more so wet in wet. However Maharshal in Or Zarua regarding eggs above siman 107 explains that if there are twenty eggs that became forbidden, forty-one are required to nullify them and not less — he teaches that always double is required, as implied by Rambam in Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot, and as Rabbeinu Yerucham wrote — no need to copy, for Acharonim already copied. And certainly for d'oraisa it is plain that whatever is more than two is called majority and nullified; from the entire matter of R' Yehudah who learns from davar sheyesh lo matirin — and for rabbinic "ascend" as written "blood of bull and blood of goat, blood of bull is more than goat blood and not nullified," and goat blood is not double bull blood — experience will prove only more in measure; nevertheless it would be fitting that goat blood be nullified. And I brought proof from Yerushalmi chapter 1 of Challah: R' Yehudah wrapped matzah and maror and ate — and it challenges: behold Hillel wrapped matzah and maror and ate them! And it sought to answer: here in time the Temple stands, here when the Temple does not stand; and it returned and answered: even these — R' Yehudah in Temple times would take only matzah and maror and not pesach, for both nullify one another — end Yerushalmi. In our Gemara in Pesachim the Gemara says: in this time a person should not eat matzah and maror together, for matzah is d'oraisa and maror d'rabbanan and they nullify one another — behold this apparently contradicts Yerushalmi who said one does not nullify one, and R' Yehudah acted thus in practice. But it appears requires study: certainly one does not nullify one except if he chews an olive-bulk of matzah and olive-bulk of maror — he must intend and limit when eating some of the olive-bulk of matzah that he not eat more maror and chew it; for then maror is majority and nullifies matzah, and likewise conversely; therefore he must limit that the chewing of matzah and maror be intended — not less and not more; this is difficult for the meticulous, therefore Chazal said a person should not eat them together, lest he increase one over the other and nullify it — this is for ordinary people; but R' Yehudah who was a great rabbi and God helped him was meticulous in his eating not to chew and eat more even slightly of matzah over maror, and always intended them together so nullification not occur and he fulfill the mitzvah of wrapping as Torah — and this is clear. And it is explained explicitly that one in one is not nullified — behold whatever is more is nullified, and double is not required; and Yerushalmi's words draw after them Rambam in order of Pesach: in Temple times he would wrap matzah and maror — Raavad commented: he was not precise; commentators explained it should say pesach, matzah and maror (and see responsum Sha'ar Efrayim and what the Gaon Rabbi Leib Zintz ztz"l, father of my righteous mother the famous Mrs. Sheindel z"l, wrote there). According to the above it is reconciled: Rambam ruled like R' Yochanan who disagrees with Hillel — three not to eat, for two nullify one; only one in one; and halachah follows R' Yochanan, therefore he ruled accordingly; and I elaborated elsewhere. And see this I found from Rabbeinu Shel Yisrael Maharsha who wrote in Tosafot chapter Elu Overin: the Gemara challenges — according to one who says olive-bulk per person is d'oraisa — behold in two pots, one of hullin and fell into two containers, one hullin and one terumah — we say "I say hullin fell into hullin and terumah into terumah" — and if olive-bulk per person is d'oraisa, how do we say "I say"? Tosafot challenged: behold it must deal that they were numerous, for if it deals with terumah that is d'oraisa, we conclude in chapter HaOrlah and it is numerous — if so same kind in its kind is nullified in majority. Maharsha challenged: why need proof from Orlah — from its place we learn, for it must be as we say explicitly in Nazir; and by your reasoning olive-bulk per person is not d'oraisa — behold heter combines to issur! And the Gemara answers: heter is abundant — we do not say heter combines, etc. — in any case learn that heter is more than issur. Maharsha's answer: certainly we establish it is abundant, but nevertheless heter is not double like issur and nullification does not apply to it — unlike in Orlah where abundance is required on account of nullification — learn it is double — end. And this is a great strain and wonder in my eyes, for even poskim who require double mean d'rabbanan, but d'oraisa majority alone suffices as written from bull blood and goat blood and in Tosafot's words all d'oraisa; in d'rabbanan certainly we say "I say," etc. If so our great rabbi should hold this law is d'oraisa — very difficult. And it is strained to say Maharsha's intent is there is room to err that double is required for nullification — if so Tosafot did not want to challenge from "they are abundant" perhaps to reject those who require double, therefore stronger to challenge from Orlah where there is no room to err. But in truth for practical ruling Maharsha agrees double is not required. And Maharsha's difficulty itself appears thus: Tosafot raised in Pesachim and Nazir that heter combining to issur is when heter is absorbed into issur, not stam without absorption — see there; if so one must understand what the Gemara says on two difficulties — and by your reasoning heter combines to issur, etc. — what difficulty? Perhaps it deals where fallen heter is not absorbed with issur and heter combining does not apply? Must say stam in those pots that fell into containers they will cook or bake, and behold absorbed one in another — this is clear and plain. If so it says well that they are abundant — for certainly what fell from the pot with that container that fell into it are equal in measure — in this a kav and in that a kav — otherwise one nullifies the other when you put kind into it to cook and make dough — behold those waters which are heter combine to heter here, and behold they are more than issur that fell — what of it if they are separate kinds water and flour — regarding heter not combining to issur there is no difference, heter combines to issur — all permit in it implies, and it says well they are abundant. But regarding one in majority nullified — the majority must all be its kind, for same kind in its kind is nullified in majority; but water does not combine to nullify it, for water is not its kind, and in not its kind we do not say one in two is nullified, and water does not assist at all to nullify — only flour in flour remains equal and Tosafot's difficulty does not apply; therefore Tosafot brought proof from Yevamot, and it is numerous — the explanation is its kind was abundant to nullify, and they challenged well — if so there is no d'oraisa issur, for in majority it is nullified — end. And Maharsha's difficulty is resolved. If so there is no proof here, and for all the matter is d'rabbanan as I clarified above in the words of the rabbis to be lenient — we listen that in majority anything more is nullified according to those poskim, and one should not be stringent at all; and so they rule in the house of study:
And there is one who forbids one person, etc. — and one should not challenge: R' Eliezer said if the head of one of them was offered, let all the heads be offered, etc. — and the difficulty: behold there is a mixture of definite blemish, how was it permitted to offer on the altar all the heads, and behold definite issur was offered on the altar! What difference whether a person eats all of them — what difference for the altar that all were offered? And see siman 110 where I elaborated in its resolution — see there:
Requires sixty. Terumat HaDeshen wrote in Tur Yoreh De'ah noten ta'am — if he cooks them it will give taste — it implies sixty is not required except d'rabbanan; and in Tosafot chapter Elu Overin it implies sixty is required from the Torah — end. Shach challenged: it is not so, for there it deals with flour in flour wet in wet, but in dry from the Torah one in majority is nullified — end; and Pri Chadash agreed. Since they shortened where they should have elaborated, and it is a great section in laws of issur and heter, I thought to elaborate, for the matters appear neither like this nor like that: dry in dry when not its kind — sixty is not required, but also not nullified in majority; rather an olive-bulk in the measure of chatzi pras is required — if there is so much it is nullified d'oraisa, and if not it is not nullified; and so Maharshal, and this is correct and close to the Gemara's form; and Terumat HaDeshen stated sixty not precisely — the root of the matters: Shach and his supporters hold we require olive-bulk per person; and Terumat HaDeshen and Maharshal's view: even if it does not give taste and is only dry in dry — nevertheless olive-bulk per person forbids. Now let us examine this tradition and poskim here — it is the view of Torah that decides (and behold according to Rambam an egg is presumed three olive-bulks, and Rashba's view a beit haperas is three eggs — if so olive-bulk per person is one-sixtieth and not nullified; but more is nullified — with this the Gemara's words end of Beitzah are understood: behold a kav of wheat became mixed in ten kabin of barley, etc. — and one must understand why the Gemara chose this number and not other numbers; and it is a matter — and according to the above in wheat and barley how can we say since not its kind it is nullified? True it is dry in dry as Tosafot wrote — nevertheless we require more than olive-bulk per person, and if not it is not nullified; therefore it says in ten, which is more than per-person portion — in nine it would be per person, and investigate) — there chapter Elu Overin Abbaye holds heter combines to issur d'oraisa and Rava disagrees, holding only olive-bulk per person is d'oraisa; and the Gemara challenges: two pots, one hullin and one terumah, and before them two containers one hullin and one terumah, and these fell into those — permitted, "I say hullin fell," etc.; and if olive-bulk per person is d'oraisa, how do we say "I say"? And we answer: terumah is d'rabbanan. Tosafot challenged: behold it is davar sheyesh lo matirin and nullified in majority, and in the container there is majority! And Tosafot answered: it must be said in any case, even not its kind, such as wheat flour in barley flour that is not nullified in majority — end. From this Terumat HaDeshen learned dry in dry not its kind is not nullified in majority; but nevertheless it is not yet proven sixty is required, and unintentionally he wrote sixty because sixty — who mentions its name? — only per-person portion whose measure is known as above; Shach for his approach explained that Tosafot's answer that it deals not its kind — wheat flour in barley flour — Tosafot hold flour in flour is called not wet, therefore not dry in dry; it turns out certainly for those who say flour in flour is called dry in dry, even Shach must agree per person even dry in dry flour in flour is forbidden; only for poskim who disagree that it is wet in wet — one must understand how per person applies only wet in wet, behold the entire difference between wet and dry is that wet gives noten ta'am — if so four kinds of media that have no taste as Tur Orach Chaim siman 442 wrote — per person does not apply, behold it is dry in dry; difficulty in Gemara: we say explicitly "leave the kuta" etc. — there is no per person, it implies they are obligated on it on Pesach, and behold they are dry in dry that give no taste at all — nevertheless they forbid per person. In truth also in Rashi Pesachim 45 one may deduce: rabbis who disagree on kuta — they have taste like essence d'oraisa, and nevertheless we say per person, and behold they are like dry in dry — what will taste add, behold taste like essence is nothing; however this is not a difficulty — we require both taste and substance as we say in Avodah Zarah: therefore taste wet does not forbid substance wet also does not forbid, for it is dry in dry — taste and substance which are two per person, and taste forbidden d'oraisa; but from Torah proof as above there is no two, for it is only kuta itself, and nevertheless we say per person d'oraisa — learn also in dry; and one may strain that kuta's explanation is as Razah wrote third taste new taste — see there in any case its taste is not called, and nevertheless not dry in dry and forbids per person — but this is strained. And one should not bring proof conversely for R' Chaim Kohen who holds taste like essence Torah specifically when there is per person; and difficulty: why taste like essence — without taste from here it would only be dry in dry, and if per person it forbids — will it lessen through noten ta'am? If so what difference whether taste like essence d'oraisa or not? It is not difficult: on account of taste like essence one need eat only olive-bulk from mixtures, unlike per person where he is not lashed until he eats all six olive-bulks; and also if mixed in more than six olive-bulks it is half measure and not nullified and forbidden, unlike dry in dry if more it is nullified. And one should not challenge what taste like essence forbids half measure even through mixtures — if more than olive in six olive-bulks mixed, nevertheless forbidden as Tur wrote siman 98 — see there. But in dry per person if mixed in more than per person — permitted since it is in mixture, and half measure through mixture we do not say. And in truth for R' Chaim Kohen who holds taste like essence forbids half measure even through mixtures — likewise dry in dry regarding per person — if so dry in dry that became mixed would forbid even in a thousand issur in a hundred heter — what he said is half measure in mixture; granted in wet in wet regarding taste like essence we say since taste was nullified there is no longer issur measure, for the root of issur which is taste was nullified — this does not apply in dry apparently, and if so even a trace would forbid. And in my novellae I said: that half measure through mixture that Rambam holds does not forbid (and see Tosafot chapter Elu Overin s.v. Le'inyan chametz and Maharsha there) — the reason is because all taste of half measure forbidden is because it is fit to combine; this applies in substance but not when mixed and nullified, for combining does not apply — it was already nullified; but return and revive applies well — fit to combine if more issur falls within mixtures and it returns and revives and there is measure. And many authors' view as above siman 98: in wet in wet we say return and revive, but not in dry; and R' Chaim Kohen may hold thus, therefore taste like essence that forbids half measure even in mixture, for it is fit to combine in addition of issur and returns and revives — unlike dry where no return and revive and fit to combine does not apply, therefore does not forbid half measure through mixture — and requires study. This is what I said in my novellae. But the essence: Torah did not be stringent in dry more than noten ta'am — if nullified it will be permitted, for its taste will not be sensed — issur is nullified even in dry even though its taste stands by itself; nevertheless in dry we are not stringent on half measure; therefore in truth Maharai's view in dry in dry not its kind in sixty — half measure is forbidden d'oraisa, only they were more stringent than sixty — how noten ta'am in cooking at all; therefore he chose the language sixty; and in truth the essence that Torah innovated taste like essence is so one need not eat all the olive-bulks. And behold Terumat HaDeshen brought proof from Tosafot chapter Elu Overin and Pesachim — and apparently in Pesachim there is no mention except surrounding to nullify Shach and Pri Chadash's law who explained in Tosafot it deals not its kind wet in wet — on this all his difficulty: if so what is the Gemara's difficulty from per person — behold in per person taste like essence d'oraisa and we find no disagreeing in Tosafot; and Tosafot raised this difficulty in chapter Gimmel Heh and there answered it deals same kind in its kind; but in Pesachim if not its kind — then the difficulty is in place. And thus it is established not like Shach who deals dry in dry, and my proof from Maharai is solid proof it does not deal wet in wet. And behold otherwise Terumat HaDeshen has proof from Gemara Zevachim chapter HaTa'aruvot: R' Eliezer said pigul, notar and tamei — he blended them one with another and ate them — exempt, for it is impossible that one not be more than the other and nullify them; and the Gemara challenges: and noten ta'am in majority is not d'oraisa! And we taught: one who makes dough from wheat and rice — if it has taste of grain it is eighteen on Pesach, etc. — and this is the refutation of the Rav Shach and supporters: why does it challenge — behold R' Eliezer deals that he ground one with another in dry until well blended — if so permitted, for it is dry in dry; but dough which is wet in wet forbids and depends on noten ta'am and taste like essence — if so even dry in dry not its kind forbids, and it challenges well that there is noten ta'am in majority. In truth also for Terumat HaDeshen's view there must be resolution why it challenges R' Eliezer from dough, etc. — perhaps there the taste is because taste like essence and this is d'oraisa for all without disagreeing; but here it is dry in dry and the issur is on account of per person — perhaps R' Eliezer does not hold like Abbaye and perhaps R' Chaim Kohen's approach; and one may say Terumat HaDeshen follows R' Chaim Kohen's approaches that taste like essence is when mixed per person — if he eats all he is liable even on olive of noten ta'am; if so the Gemara challenges well: since they are fit if there is taste, etc. — taste like essence d'oraisa — learn this law of olive per person d'oraisa, for they depend on each other as written — if so difficulty for R' Eliezer, for behold it is per person; and Terumat HaDeshen's words are compelled. And accordingly apparently also the above difficulty is resolved that we challenged Shach's view how Tosafot can explain those two containers wet in wet — then difficulty from per person, behold taste like essence! One may say Tosafot in Pesachim hold like R' Chaim Kohen, and if so according to him we do not say per person — taste like essence also we do not say one with its fellow (and Abbaye who does not hold per person nevertheless says in Chullin taste without substance d'oraisa forbidden after receiving from Rava; and further according to his words that taste like essence from meat in milk even in less than per person forbids like meat in milk — only Rava rejected his words — requires study); but after investigation there is no root, for since R' Chaim holds through mixture nevertheless half measure is forbidden — if so if olive mixed in seven olives, likewise forbidden from Torah, only no lashes; if so even though no per person d'oraisa, nevertheless if one in one mixed certainly d'oraisa one who eats is lashed even though per person is not d'oraisa (and see Tosafot Nazir who wrote explicitly); if so more than one in one is half measure and its mixture also forbids, and still one may say taste like essence for issur and not for lashes — if so even though we do not say per person d'oraisa, nevertheless taste like essence applies for half measure — still the child will say it is taste like essence. Nevertheless there is no contradiction to Zevachim where we say they depend on each other — one may say for fulfilling matzah obligation if it is only issur without lashes it suffices. And further the difficulty for R' Eliezer who holds half measure permitted from Torah — if so plainly if olive mixed in more there is no d'oraisa issur — how fulfill matzah obligation, and thus per person d'oraisa and there is lashes issur in full measure. And more plausible according to Terumat HaDeshen that sugya there goes thus and Maharsha's difficulty why challenge from dough and not from taste like essence generally is also resolved — he certainly did not want to challenge and prove per person from taste like essence what connection — only thus he proved "one who makes dough" — if so he puts wheat flour and rice flour, blends them, puts water and makes dough, and afterward bakes — then immediately at blending time wheat flour was nullified in rice flour, for in its majority nullified, and taste of wheat in rice does not yet exist, for it is cold; if so what helps afterward when baking dough and taste this in that — behold already nullified, and rice flour is called; will taste return and revive to permit? Therefore must say dry in dry not its kind was not nullified; if so before baking wheat flour was not nullified; therefore if after baking there is wheat taste — permitted, for we require wheat taste; if so difficulty for R' Eliezer, for it is proven dry in dry not nullified in majority like Terumat HaDeshen, therefore he did not challenge from taste like essence generally. And behold proof for Shach from Tosafot Chullin 86 where they challenged in any case if not its kind it should forbid taste like essence, and if its kind behold nullified in majority; and difficulty: perhaps it deals per person and nevertheless wanted the Gemara not to challenge — say it deals dry in dry mixed unrecognizably — if so why does Gemara challenge from two pots — behold dry in dry nullified in majority! Therefore must say the Gemara holds such dry in dry does not exist in reality, and they challenged well from taste like essence — if so Shach's words are compelled apparently. However Terumat HaDeshen appears to have been precise in his law from these Tosafot words: Tosafot answered it deals same kind in its kind, and nevertheless challenges — if per person in not its kind, even in its kind there should be decree lest not its kind, and Maharsha challenged: if so even though per person is not d'oraisa, nevertheless in its kind there should be forbidden decree lest not its kind that is forbidden on account of taste like essence — see there he strained to distinguish; but one may say simply: granted in stam if it deals not its kind there is difficulty how mixture is possible — behold recognizable — must say flour in flour; Tosafot hold flour in flour is called wet in wet and they challenged well — behold taste like essence d'oraisa; but after Tosafot answered it deals same kind in its kind — one may well say it deals wheat in wheat and the like that are not recognizable, for it is same kind in its kind — if so taste like essence does not apply at all; and requires study on Maharsha's difficulty that in dry in dry taste like essence does not apply even not its kind; and see below siman 111 what Rashba's words prove likewise like Terumat HaDeshen — see there. And behold Rambam chapter 9 of Hilchot Ma'achalot Assurot wrote: milk curd that fell into grits and all dissolved — those who taste the grits, if they do not find milk taste — permitted; if they find milk taste and its substance was there — behold they are forbidden from the Torah; taste without substance permitted d'rabbanan. How is its substance? Such as there was from the milk olive-bulk in every three eggs mixed — if he ate three eggs, since there is olive-bulk of milk in them he is lashed, for behold taste of issur substance exists, etc. — end. From this it implies we require two per person and taste like essence; but dry in dry where per person alone does not forbid d'oraisa; and even if strained to say dry in dry is preferable because taste stands by itself — but in wet in wet if taste is not sensed it was gone; one may say likewise in Raavad who holds "one who makes wheat from rice," etc. — meaning there is per person and he eats all six olive-bulks. And difficulty: since per person d'oraisa and he eats all six olive-bulks — why need taste of grain? According to the above it is reconciled: granted in dry issur stands by itself and preserves taste by itself — unlike wet that may lose taste and be nullified except one may say so in Raavad; nevertheless difficulty to say so in Rambam — he should have copied this law of dry in dry per person d'oraisa and lashes on it. Therefore it appears more that he holds like Rashi in that sugya Elu Overin where we say per person d'oraisa — all according to taste like essence is not d'oraisa, and we do not learn from service except this learning per person; and we say meaning in combining taste as proven from those four media kinds kuta where there is taste — therefore Rambam ruled we require two, for taste like essence is not d'oraisa, only two — taste like essence and per person — and it is R' Yochanan's statement that he ruled thus taste and substance olive per person — we require two per person and taste; we who rule taste like essence d'oraisa learn from service — if so the above does not apply; however in Yerushalmi mentioned R' Yochanan does not hold like Hillel to wrap pesach matzah maror — for two come and nullify one, and difficulty — behold dry in dry not its kind and not nullified; perhaps only d'rabbanan stringency, or entire reason of dry in dry is not nullified per person because he eats within per person — but in eating matzah he would lose mitzvah to eat them as one without interruption only one after another — see Orach Chaim siman 478 — see there; if so even if mixed in less than per person such as one in two — at least prevents eating matzah all at once — this is not correct, therefore they forbade it; perhaps they obligated to eat them all at once learned from Hillel and R' Yochanan — requires study. For practical ruling: dry in dry olive per person forbidden from Torah according to poskim; and one may strain to say one in two means only to exclude that sixty is not required; and although Tur ruled like R' Chaim Kohen that half measure through mixture forbids — nevertheless in dry in dry he did not rule, and I already wrote above what I wrote in my novellae to distinguish:

yad_avraham.he: (סימן ק"ט בהג"ה סעיף א') ויש מחמירין להשליך א' כו'. וראיתי להפר"ח בא"ח סי' תמ"ז שהקשה ע"ד האומרים כן מדתנן במסכת ערלה הערלה וכה"כ עולין בא' ומאתים וא"צ להרים וה"ה ביבש כשנתבטל ברוב ואף באיסור הנאה וכתב על רש"י מה שאינו נכון שפירש בפ"ק דביצה גבי חבילי תלתן של כה"כ יעלו בא' ומאתים היינו שיעלה א' מהן וידלק והשאר מותרין. ונראה שנעלם ממנו מ"ש המרדכי בזה בפ"ק דביצה גבי ביטול ברוב דצריך לזרוק א' מהן ולא דמי לתרומה דהכל מעורב ביחד ואין יכול לאכול האיסור לבדו בלא תערובות חולין ולכך א"צ להסירה כ"א מפני גזל השבט ע"כ. ובזה א"ש נמי דלא תקשי על פרש"י גבי תלתן מההיא מתני' דערלה דא"צ להרים דאיירי בדברים שא"י לאכול האיסור לבדו בלא תערובות היתר משא"כ בחתיכות וחבילי תלתן:
yad_avraham.en: (Siman 109 in the hagahah seif 1) And some are stringent to throw one out, etc. — and I saw Pri Chadash in Orach Chaim siman 447 who challenged those who say so, from what we taught in tractate Orlah: orlah and likewise terumah ascend in one in two hundred and removal is not required — and the same in dry when nullified in the majority, even in issur of benefit; and he wrote on Rashi's explanation, which is incorrect, who explained in chapter 1 of Beitzah regarding bundles of fenugreek of kohanim that they ascend in one in two hundred — meaning one of them rises and the rest are permitted by burning; and it appears this was hidden from him what Mordechai wrote on this in chapter 1 of Beitzah regarding nullification in the majority, that one must throw one of them out; and it is not comparable to terumah where everything is mixed together and one cannot eat the issur alone without mixture of heter — therefore removal is not required except on account of robbing the tribe — end. And with this one may also resolve the difficulty on Rashi's explanation regarding fenugreek from that mishnah in Orlah that removal is not required — it deals with things where one cannot eat the issur alone without mixture of heter, unlike pieces and bundles of fenugreek:

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (סימן ק"ט ש"ך סק"ג) דקמח בקמח לא הוי כלח בלח וכן מבואר להדיא ברמב"ם (פי"ג הי"ד מהל' תרומות) ועי"במ"ל (פ"א הי"ד מהל' משכב ומושב):
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en: (Siman 109, Shach s.k. 3) That flour in flour is not like wet in wet, and so is explained explicitly in Rambam (chapter 13 of Hilchot Terumot) — and see Beit Yosef MeLamed (chapter 1 of Hilchot Metamei Mishkav UMoshav):

nekudot_hakesef.he: (סימן ק"ט בט"ז ס"ק ב') ומ"ש מההיא דסי' צ"ח כו'. ולפי מ"ש בש"ך סי' צ"ח סק"ח לא קשה מידי ע"ש:
nekudot_hakesef.en: (Siman 109 in Taz s.k. 2) And what he wrote from that in siman 98, etc. — and according to what Shach wrote in siman 98 s.k. 8, there is no difficulty at all — see there:

kaf_hachayim.he: א) [סעיף א'] חתיכה שאינה ראויה להתכבד וכו' אבל ראויה להככבד בין במינה בין שלא במינה לא בטלה אפי' באלף כדלעיל סי' ק"א ולקמן סי' ק"י יעו"ש. ש"ך סק"א. פר"ח או' א' לה"פ או' א' ומשכחת חתיכה הר"ל באינה מינה בהרבה מינים או שוים במראה. שפ"ד או' א' ועיין לעיל סי' ק"א או' נ"ב.
kaf_hachayim.en: a) [Seif 1] A piece that is not worthy of honor, etc. — but worthy of honor, whether in its kind or not in its kind, is not nullified even in a thousand, as above siman 101 and below siman 110 — see there. Shach s.k. 1. Pri Chadash gloss 1, Levush gloss 1; and you find a piece — meaning when not its kind among many kinds or equal in appearance. Shafan David gloss 1; and see above siman 101 gloss 52.

kereti.he:
מין במינה אבל באינה מינה צריך ס' ואפילו יבש ביבש שמא יבשלם ויתן טעם:
והאיסור וכו' החתיכה בעצמה מיקרי יבש ביבש רק הטעם שנתנה בחתיכה שבצידה מיקרי לח בלח דרך משל חתיכות איסור במין במינו לר"י דמין במינו לא בטל היינו לח בלח אבל לא יבש ביבש החתיכה עם חברתה מיקרי יבש ביבש אבל הטעם שקבלה מחברתה מיקרי לח בלח ולא בטיל:
ואינו מכירו וקמח אי הוה לח בלח או יבש ביבש יש מחלוקת בפוסקים ודעת רמב"ם דלא מיקרי לח בלח ובתוס' יש דיעות מחולקות ודעת אחרונים דהוי לח בלח ועמ"ש פלתי והואיל ואין מוכח להדיא דקמח מיקרי לח בלח ולכך במין במינו הואיל אפילו אי הוי לח בלח דבר תורה א"צ רק רוב. אין להחמיר בקמח בקמח וברובא בטל.
חד בתרי ואם ב' בג' ביבש וכן בלח שני מדות בשלשה נבוכו האחרונים והעלו ברובא בטל וע' פלתי דד"ת ודאי בטל רק מדרבנן דעת הרמב"ם ורש"ל להחמיר דכנגד ג' בעינן ששה. ויש להקל הואיל דהוא רק דרבנן.
אבל לא יאכל וכו' דאכל ודאי איסור דנתערב אבל באוכל בפ"ע י"ל על כל אכילה היתר אכל ולכך בתערובות ב' בג' אסור ד' ביחד דאוכל איסור ודאי וכן א' בג' מותר לאכול בפ"ע ופשוט.
אפי' זה וכו' עיין פלתי דזה חומרא דרבנן ומהתורה מותר אפילו אדם אחד
ואינו מכירו דהיינו שנפרך לחתיכות קטנות שאין ניכר
יבש ביבש דעת הש"ך ופר"ח דהוא מדרבנן ותה"ד דעתו דד"ת בס' ועמ"ש פלתי ועיקר אם נתערב כזית בכא"פ שהוא נערך א' בט' זתים אסור מהתורה אבל ביותר מזה אינו רק מדרבנן דשמא יבשלם ויתן טעם
בין האיסור עיין ש"ך דהביא דעת א"ז באיסור דרבנן חד בחד מותר לאוכלן שני בני אדם אבל לא באדם אחד ורמ"א כתב שהרא"ש חולק ועיין פלתי
מדרבנן מין בא"מ יבש ביבש באיסור דרבנן דעת הש"ך חד בתרי בטל דאף אם יבשל לא יבא לידי איסור התורה והרב בעל מנחת כהן השיגו ולפי מש"ל בלא"ה יש לאסור יבש ביבש בלי הטעם שאם יבשל וכו' פשיטא דעיקר כש"ך וכן מורים דברי רמ"א
kereti.en:
Same kind in its kind; but when not its kind, sixty is required, and even dry in dry — lest he cook them and it give taste:
And the issur, etc. The piece by itself is called dry in dry; only the taste that it gave to the piece beside it is called wet in wet — by way of parable: issur pieces in same kind in its kind according to R' Yehudah — in its kind it is not nullified, meaning wet in wet; but not dry in dry — the piece with its fellow is called dry in dry, but the taste it received from its fellow is called wet in wet and is not nullified:
And one does not recognize it; and flour — if it were wet in wet or dry in dry — there is dispute among poskim; Rambam's view is that it is not called wet in wet; in Tosafot there are divided opinions; Acharonim's view is that it is wet in wet; and see what Peleti wrote; and since it is not proven explicitly that flour is called wet in wet, therefore in same kind in its kind — even if it were wet in wet, from the Torah only majority is required — one should not be stringent with flour in flour, and in the majority it is nullified:
One in two; and if two in three — in dry, and likewise in wet, two measures in three became mixed — the last ones rose in the majority and are nullified; and see Peleti that from the Torah certainly nullified, only d'rabbanan according to Rambam and Rashal to be stringent that against three we require six; and one may be lenient since it is only d'rabbanan:
But he may not eat, etc. — for eating certainly issur that became mixed; but when eating by itself, one may say regarding each eating it is heter — therefore in mixtures of two in three, forbidden all four together, for he eats certain issur; and likewise one in three — permitted to eat by itself, and it is plain:
Even this, etc. See Peleti that this is a d'rabbanan stringency, and from the Torah permitted even one person:
And one does not recognize it — meaning it was broken into small pieces that are not recognizable:
Dry in dry — Shach's and Pri Chadash's view that it is d'rabbanan; and Terumat HaDeshen's view that from the Torah sixty is required; and see Peleti; and the essence: if an olive-bulk became mixed in each piece that is the measure of one in nine olive-bulks — forbidden from the Torah; but in more than that it is only d'rabbanan, lest he cook them and it give taste:
Between issur — see Shach who brought Or Zarua's view that in d'rabbanan issur, one in one — permitted for two people to eat them, but not one person; and Rama wrote that Rosh disagrees; and see Peleti:
D'rabbanan — same kind when not its kind, dry in dry, in d'rabbanan issur — Shach's view: one in two is nullified, for even if he cooks, he will not come to Torah issur; and the Rav, author of Minchat Kohen, challenged him; and according to what I wrote above, one should forbid dry in dry without the concern that if he cooks, etc. — plainly the essence is like Shach, and so poskim rule Rama's words:

mateh_yehonatan.he: (סימן ק"ט בש"ע סעיף א') אבל לא יאכל שלשתן בב"א כו'. וי"ל הא דפריך הגמ' בריש פרק כל הזבחים שנתערבו ונבטיל ברובא הא לפמ"ש המחבר דאף דאמרינן חד בתרי בטיל מ"מ אסור לאכלו כולם כאחד וא"כ התם לגבי מזבח אם יקריבו כולם יהיה כאדם א' דאסור להקריב וי"ל דאין האיסור הקרבה אלא על הכהן המקריב וא"כ אפשר להקריב ע"י ב' או ג' כהנים שיקריבו זה אחר זה:
mateh_yehonatan.en: (Siman 109 in Shulchan Arukh seif 1) But he may not eat all three together, etc. — and one may say: that which the Gemara challenges at the beginning of chapter Kol HaZevachim SheNis'arevu and nullified in the majority — if so, according to what Mechaber said that even though we say one in two is nullified, nevertheless forbidden to eat them all as one — if so there regarding the altar, if they offer them all it would be like one person who is forbidden to offer; and one may say that the issur of offering is only upon the kohen who offers, and if so it is possible to offer through two or three kohanim who offer one after another:

mechaber.he: יבש ביבש שנתבטל חד בתרי אם בשלן כולן כאחד ואפי' לאכול כל א' בפני עצמו אסור אם אין שם ששים מפני שהרוטב בנותן טעם ונבלע בחתיכות ואם רוצה לבשלן יחד ואין שם ס' מותר להרבות עליהם כדי שיעור ששים ולבשלן ואין בו משום מבטל איסור: הגה וי"א דאם נודע התערובת קודם שנתבשלו ביחד הכל שרי דאין חוזרין ונאסרים מאחר שנתבטל ביבש (טור בשם הרא"ש ור' ירוחם בשם התוספות וכתב שכן עיקר) ובמקום הפסד יש לסמוך אדברי המקילין ולהתיר:
mechaber.en: Dry in dry that was nullified one in two — if they cooked them all as one, and even to eat each one by itself — forbidden if there is not sixty, because the gravy is noten ta'am and is absorbed in the pieces; and if he wants to cook them together and there is not sixty — permitted to increase upon them so that there is a measure of sixty and to cook them, and there is no concern of nullifying issur: {Rama: And some say if the mixture was known before they were cooked together — all is permitted, for they do not return and become forbidden after they were nullified dry (Tur in name of Rosh and R' Yerucham in name of Tosafot, and he wrote that so is primary); and in a place of loss one may rely on the lenient and permit.}

siftei_kohen.he:
ואם רוצה לבשלן כו'. מיהו לבשלן בב' קדרות שרי ואפילו בשלם בב' קדרות קודם שנודע התערובות מותר לאכלן אח"כ שהרי הרשב"א מחמיר כשבשלן יחד אפילו בשלן אחר שנודע התערובות והתיר בבישל מקצתן לצד אחד ומקצתן לצד אח' כמ"ש ב"י משמו עכ"ל הב"ח) ולפעד"נ דהא דמתיר הרשב"א בבשלן בב' קדרות היינו משום דכיון דנודע ונתבטל מן התורה וגם מדרבנן ברוב אלא דלבשלן יחד אסור משום שחזר האיסור ונתערב עם ההיתר והרי הוא כשאר איסורים הנבללים כדכתב הרשב"א להדיא ואסור אז מדרבנן והלכך כל שנתבשל בב' קדרות דלא חזר להיות כשאר איסורים הנבללים ובשעה שאוכל כל קדרה וקדרה שנתבשל בה אומר האיסור בקדרה אחרת מותר ואפילו תימא דמידי ספיקא לא נפקא מ"מ ה"ל ספיקא דרבנן לקולא ואפשר אפילו ספיקא דרבנן ליכא דאפשר דלא גזרו רבנן מין במינו בס' אלא בלח ממש אבל כשנתבטל כבר ברוב לא החמירו אח"כ ואוקמא אדאורייתא (כל שי"ל שאני אומר כו') אבל כשלא נודע התערובת דאז לא נתבטל האיסור כלל ואסור מן התורה אלא דעתה בשעת הבישול נודע התערובת א"כ על כל קדירה י"ל שמא האיסור בזו ה"ל ספיקא דאורייתא ולחומרא ואסור לכ"ע ודינו כדלקמן ס"ס קי"א דב' קדרות של אדם אחד מצטרפים לבטל בס' ע"ש:
ואין בו משום מבטל איסור. כיון שכל אחד מותר בפני עצמו ר"ן שם:
siftei_kohen.en:
And if he wants to cook them, etc. However to cook them in two pots is permitted; and even if they cooked them in two pots before the mixture was known — permitted to eat them afterward; for Rashba is stringent when they cooked them together, even if they cooked them after the mixture was known; and he permitted when he cooked some on one side and some on the other side, as Beit Yosef wrote in his name — end of Bach's words) — and in my humble opinion: that which Rashba permits to cook them in two pots is because since it was known and nullified from the Torah and also d'rabbanan in the majority — only to cook them together is forbidden because the issur returned and became mixed with the heter, and behold it is like other blended issurim as Rashba wrote explicitly, and forbidden then d'rabbanan; therefore all that was cooked in two pots did not return to be like other blended issurim, and when eating each pot that was cooked in it he says the issur is in the other pot — permitted; and even if you say no safek emerges, nevertheless it is safek d'rabbanan for leniency; and it is possible even safek d'rabbanan does not exist, for perhaps the rabbis did not decree same kind in its kind in sixty except in actual wet — but when already nullified in the majority they were not stringent afterward, and we establish it on d'oraisa ("whatever I say 'I say'," etc.); but when the mixture was not known, then the issur was not nullified at all and is forbidden from the Torah — only now at the time of cooking the mixture was known; if so, regarding each pot one may say perhaps the issur is in this one — it is safek d'oraisa for stringency and forbidden for all; and its law is as below siman 111 that two pots of one person combine to nullify in sixty — see there:
And there is no concern of nullifying issur. Since each one is permitted by itself — Ran there:

turei_zahav.he:
ואין בו משום מבטל איסור. כיון שכל אחד בפני עצמו מותר אין כאן איסור:
וי"א אם נודע כו'. משום דכבר נקרא עליו שם היתר:
turei_zahav.en:
And there is no concern of nullifying issur. Since each one by itself is permitted, there is no issur here:
And some say if it was known, etc. Because the name of heter was already called upon it:

baer_heitev.he:
להרבות. כתב הב"ח מיהו לבשלן בב' קדרות שרי ואפילו בשלן בב' קדרות קודם שנודע התערובות מותר לאכלן אח"כ והש"ך חולק ע"ז ופסק דאף בב' קדרות לא שרי אלא כשבשלן לאחר שנודע התערובות דאז היה עליו שם היתר אבל לא קודם שנודע וכו' ע"ש:
מבטל. כיון שכל א' מותר בפני עצמו הר"ן. אסור לבטל איסור בשבת או ביו"ט דאין לך תיקון גדול מזה אבל מותר לשער בס' אפילו נתערב בע"ש ולא נודע לו עד השבת. מיהו יבש ביבש שנתערב מותר להשליך א' בשבת דאינו אלא חומרא בעלמא לא הוי כמתקן. מגן אברהם באורח חיים סי' שכ"ג:
baer_heitev.en:
To increase upon them. Bach wrote: however to cook them in two pots is permitted; and even if they cooked them in two pots before the mixture was known — permitted to eat them afterward; and Shach disagrees on this and ruled that even in two pots it is not permitted except when they cooked them after the mixture was known, for then the name of heter was upon it — but not before it was known, etc. — see there:
Nullifying issur. Since each one is permitted by itself — Ran. Forbidden to nullify issur on Shabbat or Yom Tov, for there is no greater repair than this; but permitted to estimate with sixty even if it became mixed on Erev Shabbat and he did not know until Shabbat. However, dry in dry that became mixed — permitted to throw one out on Shabbat, for it is only a general stringency and is not considered repair. Magen Avraham in Orach Chaim siman 323:

beer_hagolah.he:
הרשב"א בת"ה כנוסחא שהיה לפני הב"י וכמ"ש בשם תשובת הרשב"א שצוה לתקן בת"ה מ"ש בתחלה והעתיקו הטור וכ"ב הר"ן בפ"ז דחולין:
הר"ן שם בשם הרא"ה:
beer_hagolah.en:
Rashba in Torat HaBayit in the version that was before Beit Yosef, and as he wrote in name of responsum of Rashba who commanded to emend in Torat HaBayit what he wrote at first, and Tur copied it, and so wrote Ran in chapter 7 of Chullin:
Ran שם in name of הרא"ה:

beur_hagra.he:
יבש ביבש כו'. כ"כ הרשב"א וכשיטתו שטעם ההיתר משום דכ"א אמרינן זהו ההיתר משא"כ כאן שנ"ט בכולם ואף במינו צריך מ"מ ס' מדרבנן:
(ליקוט) יבש ביבש כו'. ממ"ש בפ"ה דתרומות כשם שפחתו החולין כו' הלא"ה אסור אע"ג שכבר נתבטלה חוזר לאיסורו וערשב"א סי' תכ"ה (ע"כ):
(ליקוט) יבש כו' עתוס' דיבמות פ"ב א' בד"ה ר"י כו' א"נ כשיאפה כו' (ע"כ):
ואם רוצה כו'. כיון דהתירא נינהו וכעין זה אמרו בירושלמי פ"ד דתרומות אמתני' תאנים שחורות כו' בר פדיה אמר בוללן ומתיר כו' ואפילו חטין בחטין טוחנן ומתיר ע"ש:
וי"א כו'. כ"כ הרא"ש וכשיטתו דהאיסור נהפך להיתר ואין חוזר ונאסר וכמ"ש בזבחים ע"ג ב' אטו מניסא כו' וכמש"ל סי' צ"ט ס"ו שבדבר שהוא מדרבנן ונודע אין חוזר וניעור וז"ש ונודע כו':
beur_hagra.en:
Dry in dry, etc. So too Rashba, and according to his approach that the reason of heter is that regarding each one we say this is the heter — unlike here where noten ta'am is in all of them; and even in its kind, nevertheless sixty is required d'rabbanan:
(Likkut) Dry in dry, etc. From what is written in chapter 5 of Terumot: just as the heter decreased, etc. — the issur is forbidden even though it was already nullified, it returns to its issur; and Rashba siman 325 (end):
(Likkut) Dry, etc. — and Tosafot in Yevamot chapter 2:1 s.v. R' Yehudah, etc. Alternatively, when he bakes, etc. (end):
And if he wants, etc. Since they are already permitted; and similar to this they said in Yerushalmi chapter 4 of Terumot on the mishnah "black figs," etc. — Bar Pedayah said: blend them and permit, etc.; and even wheat in wheat — grind and permit — see there:
And some say, etc. So Rosh, and according to his approach that the issur transformed to heter and does not return and become forbidden; and as written in Zevachim 73 "is it from Nisaya," etc.; and as written above siman 99 seif 6 that in a matter which is d'rabbanan and known, it does not return and revive — and this is what he meant "and known," etc.:

pitchei_teshuva.he: להשליך אחד. עיין בתשובת נו"ב תניינא חי"ד סימן מ"ז שכתב דשוב אפילו אדם אחד יכול לאכול משנים הנותרים ולא אמרינן בהא איסורא ברובא אישתייר ע"ש:
pitchei_teshuva.en: To throw one out. See in responsum Noda BiYehudah Tinyana part 14 siman 47, who wrote that again even one person may eat from the two remaining pieces and we do not say here that issur remains in the majority — see there:

peleti.he: צריך ס' כתב הרמ"א בת"ח כלל ל"ט סי' ב' בשם הגהות א"ז הא דבעינן בדבר יבש חד בתרי היינו באיסור תורה אבל בדרבנן אפי' לא נתערב אלא חד בחד מותרים לשני ב"א או א"י וישראל לאוכלן ע"כ וכתב הרב בת"ח והרא"ש פ"ק דביצ' חולק ע"ז עכ"ל. ותמהו כל המפרשים דלא מצינו בהרא"ש פרק הנ"ל שום סתירה וזכר כלל. ונראה דאמרינן בפ"ק דביצה עצים שנשרו בי"ט לתוך התנור מרבה עליהם עצים ומבטלן וכו' ופריך הא קמבטל איסור לכתחלה ומשני ה"מ בדאורייתא אבל בדרבנן מבטלין ולרב אשי דאמר כל דבר שיש לו מתירין אפילו בדרבנן לא בטל מא"ל ה"מ היכי דאיתא לאיסורא בעינא אבל הכא מיקלי קלי לאיסורא עכ"ל. ודעת רשב"א דהך שנויא בדרבנן מבטלין איסור קאי מדלא קאמר אלא בהך תי' דמקלי קלי ולא אתי רק לתרוצי הך קושיא דדשיל"מ דמי לשל תורה אבל גוף תי' קאי בדרבנן מבטלין. אבל הרא"ש כתב דוקא בעצים דמקלי קלי לאיסורא מבטלין איסור דרבנן אבל בעלמא אפילו איסור דרבנן אין מבטלין. ויש להבין מנ"ל להרא"ש זה הסברא מה דלא משמע כן בגמרא וצ"ל דקשי' ליה קושי' תוס' שם ד"ה וכו' דהקשה מהך דליטרא קציעות עיגול בעיגולים יוסיף עליו ויבטלם ותי' התו' לחלק בין מה שעיקרו מן התורה או לא וזהו דחיקו ליה להרא"ש ולכך מפרש דאין מבטל רק היכי דמיקלי וכו' וכ"כ מהרש"א דהרא"ש מיישב קושי' תוס' והנה לפ"ד הגהת א"ז לא קשה מידי בשלמא איסור דרבנן שנתערב חד בחד א"כ לשני בני אדם מותר א"כ אין כאן שום איסור דמה בכך דאסור לאדם א' הא לב' שרי ואין כאן שום איסור גמור עד שנאמר עליו אין מבטלין איסור אבל גבי תרומה לא שייך דינו של א"ז דהא אסור התרומה עד שיעלה בא' ומאה וא"כ שם איסור עליו ואין מבטלין איסור ולא קשה מידי ואין צריך הרא"ש לומר דלא קאי בכל איסורי דרבנן ועל כרחך צריך לומר דלא סבירא ליה להרא"ש סברת הא"ז ודבריו מוכרחים למאוד ודו"ק:
peleti.en: Requires sixty. Rama wrote in Turei Chayim general rule 39 siman 2 in name of Hagahot Or Zarua: that which we require in dry matter one in two — this is in Torah issur; but in d'rabbanan, even if only one in one became mixed — permitted for two people, or one Israelite and one gentile to eat them — end; and the Rav wrote in Turei Chayim and Rosh chapter 1 of Beitzah disagrees on this — end. And all commentators wondered, for we do not find in Rosh that chapter any contradiction, and he mentioned a general rule. And it appears we say in chapter 1 of Beitzah: wood that fell on Yom Tov into the oven — add wood and nullify them, etc. — and it challenges: behold he nullifies issur l'chatchila! And we answer: this applies in d'oraisa, but in d'rabbanan we nullify; and for Rava Ashi who said every davar sheyesh lo matirin even in d'rabbanan is not nullified — no, this applies where it comes to issur in substance; but here it becomes light to issur — end. And Rashba's view: that version in d'rabbanan we nullify issur refers from what he did not say except in that version "becomes light" and comes only to answer that difficulty of sheylo yimatzu that is like Torah law; but the version itself refers in d'rabbanan we nullify. But Rosh wrote: specifically with wood that becomes light to issur we nullify d'rabbanan issur; but generally even d'rabbanan issur we do not nullify. And one must understand from where Rosh got this reasoning, for it does not appear so in the Gemara — must say the difficulty of Tosafot there s.v. Vechi challenged from a litra of dried figs — add and nullify them; and Tosafot answered to distinguish whether its essence is from Torah or not — this strained Rosh, therefore he explains we nullify only where it becomes light, etc.; and so Maharsha — Rosh resolves Tosafot's difficulty. And behold according to Hagahot Or Zarua there is no difficulty at all: granted d'rabbanan issur that became mixed one in one — permitted for two people — if so there is no issur at all — what of it that forbidden for one person, behold for two permitted, and there is no complete issur until we say one may not nullify issur; but regarding terumah his law of Or Zarua does not apply, for terumah is forbidden until it ascends one in a hundred — if so there is issur upon him and one may not nullify issur, and there is no difficulty, and Rosh need not say it does not refer to all d'rabbanan issurim; and perforce one must say Rosh did not accept Or Zarua's reasoning, and his words are very compelled — and requires study:

yad_avraham.he: (שם) ואין חילוק בכל זה בין אם האיסור מדאורייתא או מדרבנן. ב"י מסיק הש"ך ואולי הג"ה קאי אמ"ש דבעינן חד בתרי עיי"ש. והא ראייה דמקור הג"ה מהב"י ושם איתא הכי להדיא בסוף הסימן ע"ש. דהשיג אמ"ש הש"ד דבאיסור דרבנן חד בחד סגי. אלא דאין חילוק בזה עיין מהרש"א פ"ג דפסחים ונ"ל שכ"ד הרמב"ם פי"ג מהל' תרומות הלכה י"א [וכ"כ פ"ו מהל' ביכורים דין י"ב וע"ש בכ"מ שכוונתי לדעתו בעז"ה] גבי תרומת ח"ל דרבנן דחד בחד סגי וסמך אירושלמי שהביאו תוס' במנחות (ס"ז:) והראב"ד בהשגות חולק עליו וס"ל דרוב בעינן והכי מוכח לפע"ד בש"ס פג"ה (דף צח) דאמרינן שם לא תזלזל בשיעורי דרבנן ופרש"י אפילו דבר שאיסורו מדרבנן לא תזלזל בשיעורו. וכ"כ הפוסקים והט"ו סי' צ"ח ס"ו ומשמע דכל השיעורין קאמר בין שיעור ס' בלח ובין שיעור רוב ביבש לא תזלזל והרמב"ם לטעמיה אזיל שגם לענין ס' בלח זלזל באיסורין דרבנן וס"ל דאיסור מן המנין. אבל כבר השיג עליו הרשב"א וכ"פ הט"ו סי' צ"ח דבכל איסורין דרבנן דבעי' ס' בלח אין האיסור מן המנין זולת כחל ר"ס צ' וסי' צ"ח ס"ח. א"כ ה"ה לענין ביטול יבש ברוב נמי לא מזלזלינן וק"ל. נ"ל דאם נתערב חד בחד ואח"כ נפרר חתיכה א' לב' אסור דדילמא האיסור נפרר. ואפי' אם ניתוסף אח"כ חתיכה של היתר דאי לא היה נפרר היה שרי כמ"ש הג"ה סימן צ"ב ס"ה דלא אמרי' חתיכה נ"נ ביבש ואי ניתוסף היתר שרי. אבל כאן אסור דדילמא איסור נפרר ואין כאן רוב היתר. וכמ"ש סי' ק"א ס"ו שאין תולין להקל ה"נ דכוותה ע"ש ודו"ק. ונ"ל עוד שאם נתערבה חתיכה הראויה להתכבד בה עם ב' חתיכות היתר דקיי"ל ר"ס ק"א שאינה בטילה ואח"כ נחתכה א' מהן לב' דאסור ממ"נ אם היא היתר הרי האיסור עדיין בשלימות שר"ל ואינו בטל. ואפי' אם תמצי לומר שהאיסור נחתך אין להתיר שהרי אין כאן רוב חתיכות היתר כדי לבטלה שהרי נתרבה א' של איסור דקיי"ל חוזר וניעור אף ביבש סי' צ"ט ס"ו בהג"ה. ואפי' נתרבה מתוכו כדמוכח בפ"ה דתרומות והב"י ס"ס הנזכר גבי סאה תרומה שנפלה לפחות ממאה חולין טחנו והותירו כו' ע"ש ודו"ק. ומ"ש סי' ק"א דכל הנחתכות מותרות היינו שנשאר עדיין רוב חתיכות היתר וכדמוכח שם דלא התיר אלא בממ"נ ע"ש. משא"כ כשאין רוב אין ממ"נ: עוד נ"ל דיבש ביבש שנתערב חד בתרי ונפל מהתערובות א' לב' אחרים דתערובות הב' שרי לאדם א' לאכול כולם וא"צ להשליך. שהרי מ"מ יש כאן ס' א' דשמא אותו שנפל היתר הוא ואין כאן איסור כלל. דמה לי אם יש כאן ודאי אי' אלא שא"י אם אוכל האיסור שנפל או אם אוכל ודאי מה שנפל אלא שא"י אם הוא איסור. ועיין באשר"י פג"ה סי' ל"ח:
yad_avraham.en: (There) And there is no distinction in all this whether the issur is d'oraisa or d'rabbanan. Beit Yosef concludes Shach; and perhaps the hagahah refers to what he wrote that we require one in two — see there. But behold proof that the source of the hagahah is from Beit Yosef, and there it is stated explicitly thus at the end of the siman — see there; that he challenged what ShaDa wrote that in d'rabbanan issur one in one suffices — only there is no distinction in this; see Maharsha chapter 3 of Pesachim; and it appears that Rambam chapter 13 of Hilchot Terumot halachah 11 [and so chapter 6 of Hilchot Bikkurim law 12 — see there Kessef Mishneh that I aimed at his view with God's help] regarding terumah of chutz la'aretz which is d'rabbanan — one in one suffices, and he relied on Yerushalmi that Tosafot brought in Menachot (67:) and Raavad in hasagot disagrees and holds majority is required — and so appears to me in the Gemara Pesachim (98) where we say there "do not treat lightly the measures of the rabbis," and Rashi explained: even a matter whose issur is d'rabbanan — do not treat its measure lightly; and so poskim and Taz siman 98 seif 6 — it implies he means all measures, whether measure of sixty in wet or measure of majority in dry — do not treat lightly; and Rambam follows his reasoning that also regarding sixty in wet he treats lightly d'rabbanan issurim and holds the issur is from the set number — except challah siman 90 and siman 98 seif 8; if so, the same regarding nullification of dry in majority — we do not treat lightly, and requires study. It appears to me: if one in one became mixed and afterward one piece was broken into two — forbidden, lest the issur was broken; and even if afterward a heter piece was added — for if it had not been broken it would be permitted, as written in the hagahah siman 92 seif 5 that we do not say "the piece was lost" in dry; and if heter was added — permitted; but here forbidden, lest issur was broken and there is no majority of heter here; and as written siman 101 seif 6 that we do not rely to be lenient — here likewise — see there and requires study. And it appears further: if a piece worthy of honor became mixed with two heter pieces — we hold siman 101 that it is not nullified — and afterward one of them was cut into two — forbidden perforce: if it is heter, behold the issur is still complete, meaning standing and not nullified; and even if you say the issur was cut — one may not permit, for there is no majority of heter pieces to nullify it, for an issur piece increased, and we hold it returns and revives even in dry siman 99 seif 6 in the hagahah; and even if it increased from within, as proven in chapter 5 of Terumot and Beit Yosef at that seif regarding a se'ah of terumah that fell into less than a hundred of heter — they ground it and left over, etc. — see there and requires study. And what is written siman 101 that all that are cut are permitted — meaning heter pieces remained in majority, as proven there that he permitted only perforce — see there; unlike when there is no majority, there is no perforce. Further it appears to me: dry in dry that became mixed one in two, and one of the mixture fell into two others of the mixture of the two — permitted for one person to eat them all and need not throw out; for nevertheless there is here sixty — perhaps that which fell is heter and there is no issur at all; for what difference if there is certainly one, only one cannot know if he eats the issur that fell or certainly eats what fell, only one cannot know if it is issur; and see in Asheri Pesachim siman 38:

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (ס"א בהג"ה) אפי' יבש ביבש צריך ששים נתערב כזית בב' חתיכות שכל אחד ל' זיתים ואין ידוע איזו החתיכה היא האיסור י"ל כיון דא"נ א' מהגדולות הוא האיסור מ"מ הוי רוב אם כן לגבי חששא דשמא יבשלם דהוא רק דרבנן הוי ספק דרבנן שמא הקטן הוא האיסור אלא דאסור לבשלם (פמ"ג סק"ב בש"ד סקי"ד):
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en: (Seif 1 in the hagahah) Even dry in dry requires sixty — issur of an olive's bulk became mixed in two pieces, each of thirty olive-bulks, and it is not known which piece is the issur — one may say: since perhaps one of the larger ones is the issur, nevertheless there is a majority; if so, regarding concern lest he cook them, which is only d'rabbanan, it is a safek d'rabbanan — perhaps the small one is the issur — only forbidden to cook them (Pri Megadim s.k. 2 in ShaDa s.k. 14):

kaf_hachayim.he: ב) שם. שנתערבה באחרות מין במינה וכו' אבל שלא במינה צריך ס' כדבסמוך בהגה. ש"ך סק"ב. פר"ח או' ב' לה"פ או' ב' בל"י או' א' כריתי או' א' שפ"ד או' ב'.
kaf_hachayim.en: b) There. That became mixed with others, same kind in its kind, etc. — but when not in its kind, sixty is required, as below in the hagahah. Shach s.k. 2. Pri Chadash gloss 2, Levush gloss 2, Beit Levi gloss 1, Kereti gloss 1, Shafan David gloss 2.

kereti.he: ואם בשלן דעת הש"ך ופר"ת אם בישל קצת בקדירה זו וקצת בקדירה זו קודם שנודע התערובות א"כ יש בכל קדירה ספק איסור ואוסר משא"כ אם בישל לאחר שנודע התערובות (וע"ל סי' קי"א):
kereti.en: And if he cooked them — Shach's and Perishah's view: if he cooked some in this pot and some in that pot before the mixture was known — then in each pot there is safek issur and he forbids; unlike if he cooked after the mixture was known (and see above siman 111):
